request.spec:
Show on each person their statements, one line per statement still standing (a cancelled one is
gone), oldest first, as <statement date> <due-total>. The statements a merge or a transfer brings
over show among them, by date.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their statements, one line per statement still standing (a cancelled one is
gone), oldest first, as <statement date> <due-total>. The statements a merge or a transfer brings
over show among them, by date.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the statement lines, and three of the four `bin/e2e` tests pass. "statement lines scenario 2" still fails, and the cause is the machine's clock, not this change.

**The change**
- **Server:** `StatementSummary` now builds one line per stored statement. A cancelled statement is deleted from the store, so it drops out on its own. Lines are sorted oldest first by the date each statement shows: its as-of date, else the day it was taken. Statements on the same date stay in the order they were taken. Statements brought over by a merge or transfer are sorted in by date along with the person's own. `PersonView` sends these lines as `statements`, including in the as-of view rebuilt from history.
- **Front end:** each person row has a new "Statement lines" column. Each line is a `person-statement-line-line` element showing `<date> <due-total>`, or `n/a` when the due-total wasn't available, the same way snapshot lines work.

**Why scenario 2 fails**
The test makes a parent sheet (`<sheet>-p`) and never sets its "today". A new sheet's today defaults to the real date (`LocalDate.now()` in `SheetService.java:36`), which is 2026-11-15. The parent's rates are therefore recorded on 2026-11-15. When the test views the child sheet as of 2026-03-20, the parent's rates don't exist yet, so grade C shows `n/a` where the test expects the parent's 12.50 (and a claim due of 1.29). The test was presumably written when the real date was around March 2026.

To check that this is the only problem, I ran a throwaway copy of the spec outside the repo. It differs only in setting the parent sheet's today to 2026-03-20, and it passed in full, including the statement lines and audit records. I deleted the copy afterwards and didn't edit the real spec or anything in `bin/`. (Setting it to 2026-03-01 instead failed earlier, on a claim edit.)

**Decision for you:** I left the as-of rate lookup alone because it's outside this request. Making scenario 2 pass on today's date would mean changing how an as-of view inherits rates from a parent sheet, for example using the parent's current rates instead of its rates as of that date. That changes existing behaviour beyond statements. I can make that change if you want, or the test can be rerun with a clock set before 2026-03-20.
